customManagers.description: k3s versions in the system-upgrade-controller Plans, marked by a `# renovate:` comment on the line above `version:`. Without this manager the comments were ignored and k3s was never bumped.
The system-upgrade-controller CRD is pulled from a release asset URL, which no built-in manager reads. Track it so it moves with the manifests ref and image (see the grouping rule below).

packageRules.description: A Postgres major needs a dump and restore; the data directory isn't forward-compatible. Hold for approval on the Dependency Dashboard rather than opening a routine PR.

infrastructure/experiments/ holds time-boxed spikes that are expected to be deleted, not maintained. Pinned versions there are part of the experiment's record of what was tested, so bumping them is noise. Kept when no experiment is open, so the next one is excluded without anyone remembering to add it.
.archive/ holds configuration that's no longer deployed. Bumping versions there is noise (it produced a Ceph image PR after Rook itself was unused).

k3s can't skip a Kubernetes minor, so offer one PR per minor. The regex versioning keeps the +k3sN suffix significant (semver ignores build metadata, so a +k3s2 respin would be missed) and excludes release candidates. Merging starts a node-by-node rollout, so each bump waits on the Dependency Dashboard until someone is ready to watch it.

Longhorn and Rancher each support upgrading one minor at a time, so offer one PR per minor instead of jumping to the newest. These charts used to float and each outran the cluster's Kubernetes; exact pins plus PRs make every upgrade visible.

Every Helm chart is pinned to the version it runs. A chart major usually changes values, CRDs or behaviour, so it waits on the Dependency Dashboard until someone has read its upgrade notes. Minors and patches open PRs directly (Longhorn's minors are held by the next rule).
Traefik 24+ is Traefik v3, a separate planned migration (middleware and CRD changes). Hold the chart on 23.x until that migration lifts this cap.
A Longhorn minor (or major) upgrade changes the storage system and can't be rolled back, so it waits on the Dependency Dashboard until someone is ready to watch it. Patches still open PRs directly.

gotk-components.yaml is generated by `flux install --export`. Bumping one controller image inside it leaves Flux half-upgraded (new controller, old CRDs), so the generic kubernetes manager must not touch it. Flux upgrades come only from the flux manager, which regenerates the whole file.

Flux minors remove API versions, so each needs `flux migrate` on the cluster first. One PR per minor, and minors wait on the Dependency Dashboard. Flux 2.10 needs Kubernetes 1.35+, so hold below it until k3s reaches 1.35, then lift this cap.
See the rule above: a Flux minor or major needs `flux migrate` first.

The system-upgrade-controller CRD (release asset), manifests (?ref=) and image (images.newTag) must move together; split PRs left the CRD on v0.15.2 under a v0.16.3 controller. Group them into one PR. It runs the k3s upgrades, so it waits on the Dependency Dashboard.
Portainer agent must match the CE 2.x server.
Upgrade Portainer server and agent together.
